paragraphs: Shimon bar Kahana. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said—see his entry—“I saw Shimon bar Kahana drinking terumah wine in Akko ….” When did Shimon bar Kahana live? In R' Lazar's days, and he was supporting R' Lazar: Jerusalem Talmud, end of Hallah. Sedeh Yehoshua writes that he was certainly a priest, since he ate terumah. Perhaps Kahana is not a proper name but means “son of a priest.” Perhaps he calls him simply “the priest's son” because he is Shimon son of the deputy of the priests, who saw the Temple and its destruction. Hence he calls him simply Kahana, meaning the head of the priests. There is room to say so, because Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel saw him and reported in his name; see his entry. In Demai, chapter 3, halakhah 2: R' Shimon bar Kahana. Resh Lakish reports in his name: Jerusalem Pesahim, Ellu Overin, halakhah 2.
